study type: secondary analysis of a prospective observational study
exposure: shift times (day shifts, night shifts, hand-off times)
intraoperative noise characteristics (volume in decibels, percentage of time above safe levels (>60 dB), startle noise events, peak levels (>75 dB))
outcome: intraoperative noise levels (median noise, startle events, percentage of time above 60 dB, percentage of time above 75 dB)
type of cesarean delivery (unscheduled, urgent, STAT)
cohort: The study collected noise data from a total of 312 cesarean deliveries.
finding: Noise levels during cesarean deliveries did not significantly vary when comparing night shifts, day shifts, and hand-off times, despite significantly higher numbers of urgent and STAT cases and postpartum hemorrhages occurring during night shifts and hand-off times, and over 60% of case time exceeding recommended safe noise levels.
mod_finding: Significantly larger numbers of postpartum hemorrhages, unscheduled, urgent, and STAT cesarean deliveries occurred during hand-off times and on night shifts.
